# Code Review — 2026-07-29

- [ ] **[Security] No brute-force protection on bearer auth and public share links**
  - **Status quo:** `internal/selfhost/server.go:312` (`auth`) and `internal/selfhost/server.go:296` → `internal/selfhost/share.go:301` (`handleAccessShare`, unauthenticated `GET /s/{token}`) accept unlimited failed attempts. The `http.Server` sets timeouts and `MaxHeaderBytes` (`internal/selfhost/server.go:175`), but there is no rate limiting, backoff or failed-auth logging anywhere in the package. A self-hosted instance exposed to a LAN or the internet can be probed for share tokens and worker tokens at full request rate, silently.
  - **Proposed solution:** Add a small per-remote-IP limiter (e.g. `golang.org/x/time/rate` in a bounded LRU map, or a hand-rolled token bucket to stay dependency-light) applied in `securityHeaders` or a new `throttle` middleware wrapping `s.mux`, with a stricter bucket for `/s/{token}` and for requests that fail `Authenticate`. Emit a `slog.Warn` on repeated failures so operators can see probing in logs.
  - **Effort/Impact:** Low effort / high impact

- [ ] **[Security] Token-hash lookup uses a non-constant-time comparison**
  - **Status quo:** `internal/permissions/manager.go:45` compares the SHA-256 hex digest with `users[i].TokenHash == hash`, and `internal/selfhost/share.go:137` does the same for share tokens — while the legacy path right beside it already uses `subtle.ConstantTimeCompare` (`internal/selfhost/server.go:374`). The inconsistency is the concern: the hardened path exists but the primary path does not use it.
  - **Proposed solution:** Route both comparisons through the existing constant-time helper (export it from `permissions` or add `permissions.EqualHash`) so every credential comparison in the codebase uses one audited primitive, and add a regression test asserting no `==` comparison on `TokenHash` remains.
  - **Effort/Impact:** Low effort / medium impact

- [ ] **[UX/DX] `symdesk --version` reports a stale hardcoded version**
  - **Status quo:** `cmd/symdesk/main.go:18` hardcodes `var version = "0.7.0"`, and no build injects it — `Dockerfile:9` builds with `-ldflags="-s -w"` only, and neither the Makefile nor `.github/workflows/release.yml` sets `-X main.version`. The repo is at v0.7.2 (`release-notes.md:32`, `README.md:155` shows `"version":"0.7.2"`), while `project.yml:63` and `home-assistant-addon/symdesk/config.yaml:2` say 0.7.1. Users, `doctor`, the MCP handshake and the version-negotiating companion probes all get a wrong version string.
  - **Proposed solution:** Make the Go version build-injected (`-ldflags "-X main.version=$VERSION"` in Dockerfile, Makefile and release workflow, falling back to `debug.ReadBuildInfo()` for `go install` users), and add a CI check (or extend the existing 06-prerelease gate) that asserts `main.go`, `project.yml`, `SymDesk.xcodeproj`, and the HA add-on config all match the current tag.
  - **Effort/Impact:** Low effort / high impact

- [ ] **[UX/DX] `doctor` bypasses the CLI's error and `--json` contract via `os.Exit(1)`**
  - **Status quo:** `cmd/symdesk/commands.go:203` calls `os.Exit(1)` directly instead of returning an error, so it skips `main.go:33`'s JSON error envelope and the `exitcodes.ExitCodeFromError` mapping — every other command exits with a semantic code. The test suite explicitly documents that this makes the command untestable (`cmd/symdesk/cli_exec_test.go:70-72`).
  - **Proposed solution:** Return a typed error (e.g. `exitcodes` diagnostic-failure error) from the `RunE` instead of exiting, so `--json` emits `{"error": ...}` and the process exits with the same semantic code as the rest of the CLI; then enable the currently-skipped `doctor` assertions.
  - **Effort/Impact:** Low effort / medium impact

- [ ] **[Architecture] `cmd/symdesk/commands.go` holds ~50 commands in one 1385-line file**
  - **Status quo:** `cmd/symdesk/commands.go:1` is 1385 lines and defines roughly 50 `cobra.Command` values, while sibling command groups already follow a one-domain-per-file convention (`cmd/symdesk/meetings.go`, `history.go`, `retention.go`, `permissions.go`, `recipes.go`, `mail.go`). The file is the single largest Go source in the repo and the natural merge-conflict hotspot for parallel agent work.
  - **Proposed solution:** Split it along the conventions already present in the package — e.g. `doctor.go`, `index.go`, `search.go`, `doc.go`, `ai.go` — moving each command constructor verbatim with no behaviour change, keeping `commands.go` as the wiring that registers the groups on `rootCmd`.
  - **Effort/Impact:** Medium effort / medium impact

- [ ] **[Architecture] The shared service contract is untyped `map[string]interface{}`**
  - **Status quo:** `internal/service/service.go` returns `[]map[string]interface{}` from the core read paths (`Search`, `SearchWithMeta`, `Docs`, see `internal/service/service.go:139` and `:151`, 15 occurrences in that file alone, plus `internal/service/views.go`). These maps are the contract shared by the CLI, the MCP server and the Swift apps, so field names like `"path"`, `"title"`, `"snippet"` are stringly-typed and only checked at runtime — a rename is invisible to the compiler across three consumers.
  - **Proposed solution:** Introduce explicit result structs with JSON tags (the file already does this well for `SearchResponse` at `internal/service/service.go:132`) and return `[]SearchResult` / `[]DocResult`; keep the JSON wire shape byte-identical so MCP and Swift clients are unaffected, and migrate one call path at a time.
  - **Effort/Impact:** Medium effort / high impact

- [ ] **[Performance] Non-admin snapshots re-parse, re-marshal and re-gzip the whole vault on every request**
  - **Status quo:** `internal/selfhost/server.go:508` (`snapshotPayloadFiltered`) takes the carefully cached admin payload from `snapshotPayload` and, for every non-admin request, `json.Unmarshal`s the entire vault, filters it, re-marshals it and re-gzips it (`internal/selfhost/server.go:517-541`). None of this is cached — the ETag/dirty-flag caching built at `internal/selfhost/server.go:433` benefits admins only, so the multi-user path pays full O(vault-size) CPU and allocation on every poll.
  - **Proposed solution:** Cache the filtered payload per user keyed by `(baseETag, user.Name, permissionsGeneration)` in the existing `snapshotMu`-guarded state, invalidating on the same dirty flag plus a permissions-file mtime/generation counter. The existing `If-None-Match` handling then short-circuits repeat polls for non-admins too.
  - **Effort/Impact:** Medium effort / high impact

- [ ] **[Performance] `CanRead`/`CanWrite` re-read the permissions and groups JSON from disk on every call**
  - **Status quo:** `internal/permissions/manager.go:63` calls `m.loadPermissions()` and `:75` calls `m.loadGroups()` per invocation, and `loadPermissions` (`internal/permissions/manager.go:400`) does an uncached `os.ReadFile` + `json.Unmarshal` each time. Because `snapshotPayloadFiltered` calls `CanRead` once per note (`internal/selfhost/server.go:521`), a single snapshot request for a 5,000-note vault performs 5,000 file reads and JSON parses.
  - **Proposed solution:** Add an mtime-validated in-memory cache inside `Manager` for the rules and groups files (RWMutex + stat check, invalidated on `savePermissions`/`saveGroups`), so a request-scoped burst of permission checks costs one read. Optionally add a `CanReadMany(user, paths)` batch entry point for the snapshot path.
  - **Effort/Impact:** Low effort / high impact

## Conclusion

The repo is in good shape: constant-time legacy token comparison, CSP/nosniff security headers, server timeouts, `MaxBytesReader` upload caps, hashed-only share tokens, and a snapshot cache backed by an fsnotify watcher are all already in place — so the findings above are refinements, not fundamentals.

**Best first quick win:** fix the version drift (`cmd/symdesk/main.go:18` reports 0.7.0 while the released version is 0.7.2) by injecting the version at build time and adding a consistency check to the prerelease gate. It is a few lines, it is user-visible in `--version`, `doctor`, and the MCP handshake, and it prevents the same drift recurring at every release.
